Temesgen and von Gadow (2004) DBH–height models for interior British Columbia

Source: R/hd_temesgen2004.R
hd_temesgen2004.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the generalized height–diameter models of Temesgen and von Gadow (2004) for eight tree species of complex (mixed-species, uneven-aged) stands in the Interior Douglas-fir (IDF) biogeoclimatic zone of southern interior British Columbia. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm) alone (Model 2) or from DBH, the tree's basal area in larger trees and two stand-density predictors (Model 7).

Usage

hd_temesgen2004(
  DBH,
  species,
  BAL = NULL,
  TPH = NULL,
  BA = NULL,
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter outside bark at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PSEU.MEN"; compact "PSEUMEN" is accepted).

BAL

Optional numeric vector. Tree level. Basal area in larger trees (m²/ha): basal area per hectare of the trees larger than the subject tree in its plot (source "BAL", p. 47). The source does not state the species basis or a minimum DBH (plots recorded trees with DBH \(\ge\) 2 cm). Must be >= 0. Supply with TPH and BA to use Model 7.

TPH

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Number of trees per hectare (source "SPH", p. 47); minimum DBH not stated (plots recorded trees with DBH \(\ge\) 2 cm). Must be > 0.

BA

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Basal area per hectare (m²/ha) (source "BA", p. 47); minimum DBH not stated. Must be > 0.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("temesgen2004_m2" or "temesgen2004_m7").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): trembling aspen (POPU.TRE), western redcedar (THUJ.PLI), paper birch (BETU.PAP), Douglas-fir (PSEU.MEN), western larch (LARI.OCC), lodgepole pine (PINU.CON), ponderosa pine (PINU.PON) and the interior spruce complex. The source "spruce" combines Engelmann and white spruce (Table 1, p. 50); its coefficients are used for PICE.ENG, PICE.GLA and the hybrid PICE.ENG.GLA. Fitted to BC Ministry of Forests permanent sample plots (49°–52°30′N) from which thinned, spaced and selectively logged plots were excluded; the authors caution against using the models in such stands.

Model forms (Models 2 and 7, pp. 46–47): $$H = 1.3 + a [1 - \exp(-b \, DBH^{c})],$$ with \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) species constants for Model 2 (Table 5, p. 51), and for Model 7 (Table 4, p. 50) $$a = a_1 + a_2 BAL + a_3 TPH + a_4 BA, \quad c = a_5 + a_6 BAL.$$ Terms dropped by the authors as non-significant (blank in Table 4) are zero; e.g. Model 7 for ponderosa pine uses no stand predictor and is practically identical to Model 2.

Corrected exponent sign: both equations are printed as \(1 - e^{b D^{c}}\). With the published (positive) \(b\) this gives negative heights, so the standard Weibull form of Yang et al. (1978), \(1 - e^{-b D^{c}}\), is used. It reproduces the observed mean heights of the fitting data (Table 1).

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured outside bark at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Variants: if BAL, TPH and BA are all NULL (default), Model 2 (DBH only) is used. If all three are supplied, Model 7 is used for every species, even for species where some or all of them have no effect. Supplying only some of them is an error. A one-time message reports the variant used. Coefficients are ordinary nonlinear least-squares fits (SAS PROC NLIN); no calibration information is published.

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. DBH outside the per-species range of the fitting data (Table 1) is computed and reported in a single warning. The source gives no ranges for BAL, TPH or BA; Model 7 inputs extreme enough to make \(a\) or \(c\) non-positive raise an error.

References

Temesgen, H., and von Gadow, K. (2004). Generalized height–diameter models — an application for major tree species in complex stands of interior British Columbia. European Journal of Forest Research, 123(1), 45–51. doi:10.1007/s10342-004-0020-z

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# Model 2: DBH only
hd_temesgen2004(DBH = c(10, 25, 40), species = c("PSEU.MEN", "PINU.CON", "PICE.ENG"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   9.12
#> 2  21.8 
#> 3  27.7 

# Model 7: with basal area in larger trees, stems/ha and basal area
hd_temesgen2004(
  DBH = c(10, 25, 40),
  species = c("PSEU.MEN", "PINU.CON", "PICE.ENG"),
  BAL = c(20, 8, 2), TPH = 800, BA = 25,
  keep_model_id = TRUE
)
#> hd_temesgen2004(): `BAL`, `TPH` and `BA` supplied; using Model 7 (DBH and stand
#> variables).
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   height model_id       
#>    <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1   9.29 temesgen2004_m7
#> 2  19.9  temesgen2004_m7
#> 3  24.7  temesgen2004_m7

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18),
  species = c("PSEU.MEN", "LARI.OCC", "POPU.TRE"),
  BAL = c(18, 6, 12), TPH = c(900, 900, 600), BA = c(24, 24, 15)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_temesgen2004(DBH, species, BAL, TPH, BA))
#>   DBH  species BAL TPH BA   height
#> 1  12 PSEU.MEN  18 900 24 10.79649
#> 2  25 LARI.OCC   6 900 24 21.84368
#> 3  18 POPU.TRE  12 600 15 13.98348
